environment: Canonical candidate archive; real Java21 jar and disposable PostgreSQL18.6 on loopback. No customer records or deployment.
title: Database permits hearing chronology and reverse parent/case inconsistency
preconditions: Disposable migrated DB owner connection with normal constraints/triggers enabled
Synthetic cases A/B, proceeding P in A, hearing H in P
steps: In separate BEGIN/ROLLBACK transactions execute UPDATE proceeding SET filing_date='2026-01-04' WHERE id=P
Execute UPDATE hearing SET hearing_date='2026-01-01' WHERE id=H
Execute UPDATE proceeding SET case_id=B WHERE id=P
Compare hearing/proceeding pair inside each transaction before rollback
expected: Reject each invariant-breaking database statement; preserve dates, relation and history
actual: All three SQL statements succeed. Reverse hearing.case_id change is correctly rejected by existing trigger. API guards pass.
risk_boundary: Privileged direct SQL / trusted future writer integrity gap, not demonstrated remote API or authorization bypass. QA probes always roll back.
contract_note: Separate from fixed QAD-032 API defect; owner explicitly requested database-level integrity. Existing service guard is credited.
recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES for database-integrity acceptance; unrelated synthetic Dev/UAT development may continue

retests.note: All3 counterexamples now COMMIT with NOSUPERUSER/NOCREATEDB/NOCREATEROLE role granted only schema usage and SELECT/UPDATE on hearing/proceeding. New connection observes1 invalid row per probe. Disposable QA DB only; not a remote API authorization bypass.
